Present petition has been filed for setting aside the order issuing process against the accused/petitioner company dated 8.8.2012 and quash the complaint dated 7.12.2002 filed under Section 16(1)(a)(i) read with Section 7 .
of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 before Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (Court No.2), Shimla, being complaint case No. 9003301 of 2002 titled State of Himachal Pradesh vs.
Mansa Ram and others and consequent proceedings thereunder.

sentences.text: 2 Prosecution, against the petitioner as well as respondents No. 2 and 3, has been launched under Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 for not mentioning the details 'best before date' on whisky bottle containing more than 10% alcoholic strength as it was treated as misbranding of product.

3 In view of communication dated 3.5.2018 (Annexure P9) issued by the Head of GA/Legal, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India and an order dated 8.12.2017 (Annexure P-10) passed by the same authority, the Additional Chief Secretary to the Government of H.P. has considered the representation made by the petitioner (Annexure P-8) and has taken a decision by passing an order dated 4.6.2019, which has been placed on record by .
the office of Advocate General along with forwarding letter addressed to the Registrar General of this Court.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The operative part of the said order is as under:-
"Now, therefore, after examining the Annexure P-8, P-9 and P-10 of the petition and Regulation 2.2.2.10 of the Food Safety Standards (Packaging and Labeling)
Regulations, 2011, it has been decided to withdraw all cases filed under PFA Act, 1954 for non-mentioning of 'best before date' on whisky bottle containing more than 10%
Alcoholic strength treating the same as mis- branded.

sentences.text: In view of aforesaid, decision taken by the respondent/State, criminal proceedings based on complaint, referred above, pending before Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Shimla are liable to be closed and as per the decision of respondent-State, nothing survives to be adjudicated.

5 Copy of order has also been supplied to petitioner, DHSR H.P., Director Prosecution, District Attorney, .
Shimla for taking further necessary action.
Therefore, now necessary action for withdrawal of complaint is to be taken by the concerned authority.

However, it is made clear that in case the concerned authority fails to take appropriate action, the petitioner or its authorized representative is at liberty to place this order on record of the trial Court, whereupon the trial Court shall close the complaint in accordance with law.
6 Petition is disposed of in aforesaid terms.

opennyai_summary.facts: 2 Prosecution, against the petitioner as well as respondents No. 2 and 3, has been launched under Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 for not mentioning the details 'best before date' on whisky bottle containing more than 10% alcoholic strength as it was treated as misbranding of product.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The operative part of the said order is as under:-
"Now, therefore, after examining the Annexure P-8, P-9 and P-10 of the petition and Regulation 2.2.2.10 of the Food Safety Standards (Packaging and Labeling)
Regulations, 2011, it has been decided to withdraw all cases filed under PFA Act, 1954 for non-mentioning of 'best before date' on whisky bottle containing more than 10%
Alcoholic strength treating the same as mis- branded.
In view of aforesaid, decision taken by the respondent/State, criminal proceedings based on complaint, referred above, pending before Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Shimla are liable to be closed and as per the decision of respondent-State, nothing survives to be adjudicated.
5 Copy of order has also been supplied to petitioner, DHSR H.P., Director Prosecution, District Attorney, .
Shimla for taking further necessary action.
Therefore, now necessary action for withdrawal of complaint is to be taken by the concerned authority.
However, it is made clear that in case the concerned authority fails to take appropriate action, the petitioner or its authorized representative is at liberty to place this order on record of the trial Court, whereupon the trial Court shall close the complaint in accordance with law.
6 Petition is disposed of in aforesaid terms.
